newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Congress to pass petrochemicals, fuel laws soon.
newsitem.headline: Congress to pass petrochemicals, fuel laws soon.

text.p: The Venezuelan Congress is due to revise by December a law that allows state oil company Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA) to participate in all petrochemicals operations, a senior minister said on Friday.
Deputy Energy and Mines Minister Evanan Romero told Reuters the Congress in Caracas was also due to approve by December a law opening the domestic hydrocarbons market to competition.
He was speaking in the margins of a conference on trade and investment opportunities in Venezuela's energy and petrochemicals sectors, organised by the Belgian Foreign Trade Board.
Romero said he expected the move to end PDVSA's right to take part in all petrochemicals operations would generate substantial interest among foreign investors.
But he said PDVSA was likely to continue playing a major role in the sector.

"Even though the law will pass I think most of the foreign private investors in petrochemicals will seek the participation of our national petrochemical company because it has shown it has been run efficiently...and it will add value to an association," the minister said.

"The new law would give PDVSA the right to divest from existing equity in existing plants and use that...seed money for more developments and (operations involving) other foreign (investors)," he added.
Romero predicted this development would be "a tremendous boost" to Venezuela's petrochemicals sector.
PDVSA has entered into 17 petrochemicals joint ventures with local and international private companies since the 1970s.
The minister said plans to open up the domestic fuels market to private participation would show Venezuelans the government was serious about liberalisation.
"They will feel it every week when they fill their (petrol) tanks," he said.
He said major international oil companies had expressed great interest in the moves, including Shell, Mobil, Texaco, Exxon, British Petroleum and Total.
Romero said the government would continue to set a maximum price for domestic fuels until the end of 1998.
At present, domestic motor fuels are fixed at 85 percent of the price at which Venezuela exports fuel. -- Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6800
